blocks.html: Hyperlipidemia is an abnormally high concentration of fats or lipids (fat particles) in the blood. This can also mean that there is too much LDL (bad) cholesterol or triglycerides in the blood. This condition can increase the risk of blockages in arteries by increasing the amount of fatty deposits.
This disease typically does not have any symptoms.
Hyperlipidemia is usually diagnosed through blood tests and can be seen with the results of a cholesterol panel.

blocks.text: Common Supplements Found in Our Pharmacy to Help Lower Cholesterol and Control Hyperlipidemia

blocks.html: Niacin Niacin (vitamin B3) is one of the most effective supplements that can help raise HDL-C levels and reduce LDL-C levels and triglycerides. Talk to your doctor about how this supplement might help you lower your cholesterol.
Omega-3 Fatty Acids Taking these offer a wide variety of health benefits including the ability to reduce blood pressure by reducing the LDL, or bad cholesterol.
Soluble Fiber has been associated with lowering total cholesterol and LDL-C.

Hyperlipidemia can be prevented as well as sometimes treated by incorporating a healthy diet, weight loss, and exercise. In addition, it is a wise idea to choose foods low in trans fat and eat more fiber rich foods. Eating fish twice a week can also help prevent or treat hyperlipidemia.
For some people, diet and lifestyle changes may not be enough so their doctor will prescribe medications in order to help bring their cholesterol levels into a healthy range.
